author: BBC News
description:
Dignitaries, lawmakers, and world leaders gathered in Washington on Tuesday for the funeral of longtime Republican Senator Lindsey Graham.

After a morning memorial ceremony at the US Capitol, a formal service took place at the Washington National Cathedral.

President Donald Trump led the national tributes, calling Graham a tough senator who "went out at the peak of his career." 

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy were in attendance - the late senator was a staunch supporter of their countries.

author: BBC News
description:
Search and rescue teams are racing to find people missing at a collapsed shopping centre and a damaged paper factory after a strong earthquake hit south-western Japan.

The quake hit Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT) on Tuesday, with hundreds of thousands of people told to move to evacuation shelters. a tsunami warning was issued for Kyushu's south-western coastlines, though it was later lifted.

The second floor at the Aeon Mall shopping center in Kashima Town collapsed, trapping people inside. 

Tens of thousands of homes  were left without power. Prime minister Sanae Takaichi said officials were evaluating reports of collapsed buildings, fires, damaged roads and bridges, and power outages. She urged residents to evacuate to safe locations and remain alert.

Jane Hill presents BBC News at Ten reporting by Caroline Hawley.

Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has met with President Donald Trump in Washington DC for their first in-person talks since US airstrikes on Iran began in February.
 
The meeting comes amid signs of growing friction between the two leaders. Trump has publicly criticised Israel for continuing strikes in Lebanon and ignoring a ceasefire.
 
Meanwhile, Iran’s state broadcaster said two men who took part in nationwide anti-government protests earlier this year have been publicly executed in the city of Isfahan.
 
And elsewhere, Oman has reportedly proposed a regional system for managing the Strait of Hormuz, following technical talks with Tehran.

description:
Today, secondary school pupils in England will be offered more technical subjects as part of education reforms led by the new prime minister.

The courses, which will be available from year 10 onwards will be linked to local industries in the hope of giving children a clearer pathway into work.

Andy Burnham says he’s keen to strengthen links between education and the workplace and these reforms come alongside a new bursary scheme which aims to remove financial barriers to accessing apprenticeships.

Adam discusses the reforms, and whether they can achieve their aims, with Justine Greening, the former education secretary and founder of the Purpose Coalition which aims to improve social mobility, and Shane Chowen, editor at FE Week.

Plus, Adam catches up with By-Electioncast veterans Sarah Lester, editor of the Manchester Evening News and Kevin Fitzpatrick, political reporter at Radio Manchester to discuss the Manchester mayoral by-election, which goes to the polls on Thursday.

Laura Loomer, an ally of US President Donald Trump and a MAGA influencer, has visited Ukraine, where she was granted extensive access to the destruction caused by the war.

For years, Loomer has been a prominent critic of US assistance to Ukraine, at times labelling the country a "Nazi state". 

But after visiting the country she said she had fallen for some "Russian propaganda" and offered an apology to Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky. 

It comes as the White House says Trump has held “positive and productive” meetings with both Zelensky and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in separate behind-closed-doors meetings.

We ask the BBC's Washington correspondent Bernd Debusmann how the Democrats have changed their attitude towards Israel in light of the war in Gaza, and the conflict in Iran. 

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been meeting President Donald Trump in Washington, at a tense time for US-Israel relations. Though they entered the war with Iran as partners, President Trump has publicly criticised Israel over its handling of the conflict - even calling Mr Netanyahu "crazy" in a phone call about Israel's fight against Hezbollah in Lebanon.  

Meanwhile, more than 100 House Democrats recently voted to cut military aid to Israel. And some of the parties top figures - including California Governor Gavin Newsom and Senator Cory Booker have promised not to accept any money from the pro-Israel lobby group AIPAC.

description:
When the Trump administration announced last week that it had signed a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia, the agreement was held up by US Energy Secretary Chris Wright as evidence that ”the American nuclear renaissance is underway”. 

Although the text of the deal has not yet been made public, US media report that it could allow Saudi Arabia to enrich uranium in the future.  But shortly after the announcement, President Trump took to Truth Social to qualify the news – saying that the deal hinges on Saudi Arabia’s willingness to recognise the state of Israel.

Is that likely? And could the deal derail ongoing negotiations between the US and Iran? We speak to BBC security correspondent Frank Gardner.

Several people are trapped inside a shopping centre after a strong earthquake hit south-west Japan, officials say.
 
Some local media reports that there was an explosion at the Aeon Mall in Kumamoto, following the magnitude 7.1 earthquake.
 
The quake hit inland on Kyushu island at 16:27 local time (07:27 GMT), with more than 150,000 people being told to move to evacuation shelters. There was a brief tsunami warning that was lifted within the hour.
 
Emergency services said "many people" were trapped inside the Aeon Mall in the Kumamoto region.

author: BBC News
description:
France and Spain continue to battle wildfires, as temperatures are expected to soar past 40C in some regions in the coming days.
 
Spain's national weather service says the severe weather is forecast to last until "at least" Sunday, and warns of "extreme" fire risks as firefighters continue to battle the some of the worst blazes in the country's history.
 
France's south-west regions Gironde and Landes are under "yellow alert" for a heatwave expected to peak on Wednesday, further hampering efforts to contain "very unpredictable" blazes in Gironde.
 
The mayor of Bordeaux has said he is preparing for "all eventualities", as one of the wildfires burning in France is 15km (nine miles) from the south-western city.

description:
There is a state of emergency in Ecuador - the latest in a series - as the country battles local drug gangs with links to international cartels. Once one of South America’s most peaceful corners, Ecuador now has a murder rate that is one of the highest in the world.

The country has become the gateway for about 70% of the cocaine reaching the US and Europe – including the UK. The drug floods in from neighbouring Colombia and Peru, the two biggest cocaine producers in the world.

The BBC’s Orla Guerin has been at the heart of the war on drugs in Duran, one of the most gang-controlled cities in Ecuador.

description:
About 600,000 mosquitoes are being released across the Washington DC area this summer to help reduce local mosquito populations. 
 
Only male mosquitoes – infected with the naturally occurring bacteria Wolbachia – are released. They don't bite humans, and the bacteria they carry prevents any eggs produced after mating from hatching.
 
The release of mosquitos comes as climate change creates more favourable conditions for the insects to survive and reproduce, increasing concerns about the spread of mosquito-borne diseases.
